editorial_thesis: Agent infrastructure is becoming managed, evaluation is becoming a living evidence system, and security is following the full tool-and-data call graph.

topic_groups.title: Agent Runtimes
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fresh managed-agent infrastructure signal with direct Buildn architecture leverage and a coverage gap versus recent code-review reports.

sources.title: Introducing the Agents API
sources.why_selected: Public beta exposes durable sessions, harnesses, tools, subagents, and environments.
sources.usefulness: Provides a concrete runtime to prototype against while preserving Buildn-owned evidence contracts.

sources.title: Agents API overview
sources.why_selected: Defines Agent, Environment, Session, and Events/Items as explicit primitives.
sources.usefulness: Useful vocabulary for Buildn job state, recovery, and operator UX.

sources.title: HarnessDev
sources.why_selected: Evaluates agents that create and evolve the harness itself.
sources.usefulness: Supports treating harnesses as versioned software artifacts.

sources.title: The Unreliable Progress Bar
sources.why_selected: Tests whether agents can report execution progress reliably.
sources.usefulness: Supports evidence-based milestone UX instead of model-authored percentages.

topic_groups.title: Evaluation Radar
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Measurement is under-covered recently and the current research offers practical provenance, reliability, and continuity patterns.

sources.title: Benchmark Radar
sources.why_selected: Living catalog and search engine for benchmark artifacts and score provenance.
sources.usefulness: Can seed a maintained evaluation library for Buildn and client work.

sources.title: DAREBench
sources.why_selected: Frames evaluation around deployment-aware and reliable execution.
sources.usefulness: Adds operational constraints to capability testing.

sources.title: Persistent identity benchmark
sources.why_selected: Benchmarks identity continuity in deployed agents.
sources.usefulness: Useful for safe memory and cross-session invariants.

sources.title: Mapping benchmark design
sources.why_selected: Maps how benchmark design choices shape conclusions.
sources.usefulness: Encourages explicit blind spots and task definitions.

topic_groups.title: Agent Security + Sovereignty
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Current product and threat signals make the tool/data boundary concrete for client-safe agent deployment.

sources.title: Cisco AI Defense release notes
sources.why_selected: Adds MCP inventory, runtime inspection, red teaming, and hybrid policy enforcement.
sources.usefulness: Offers an asset and policy taxonomy for Buildn’s own inventory.

sources.title: Cisco AI Defense Python SDK
sources.why_selected: Provides application-boundary inspection for LLM, HTTP, and MCP traffic.

sources.title: Anthropic threat intelligence report
sources.why_selected: Documents current token theft, persistence, and exfiltration behaviors.
sources.usefulness: Improves worker threat models beyond prompt injection alone.

sources.title: Sovereign and air-gapped AI security
sources.why_selected: Makes residency and offline operation explicit deployment requirements.
sources.usefulness: Supports client architecture options for local and disconnected evidence paths.
